cohort: The cohort consisted of 285 pregnant women receiving high-risk prenatal care who delivered at a referral hospital in Diamantina, Minas Gerais, Brazil.
finding: Maternal obesity was associated with increased obstetric intervention, particularly cesarean delivery and induction for hypertensive disorders, though neonatal outcomes were comparable across BMI categories.
mod_finding: Obese women had significantly higher rates of cesarean delivery (64%) compared to overweight and eutrophic women.
